q: Why are neutrons slowed down with water in a light-water reactor?
a: The neutrons produced in fission are fast, but uranium-235 splits much more probably when a slow neutron hits it. Water slows neutrons as they collide with hydrogen nuclei, so the chain reaction can continue even though the fuel contains only a few percent uranium-235.

q: Why must the deuterium–tritium fuel in a fusion power plant be heated to a temperature of about $1.5 \cdot 10^{8}\,\text{K}$?
a: The nuclei are positively charged and repel each other. Only nuclei colliding at a very high speed get so close to each other that the strong interaction joins them. A high speed means a very high temperature.
